dataset_metadata.name: RWTH Aachen Calendaric Aging of NCA/Si-C 18650 (Samsung INR18650-35E) over 5 Years
dataset_metadata.institution: RWTH Aachen University, Institute for Power Electronics and Electrical Drives (ISEA)
dataset_metadata.citation: Frie, F., Ditler, H., Klick, S., Stahl, G., Rahe, C., Ghaddar, T., Sauer, D. U. (2024). An Analysis of Calendaric Aging over 5 Years of Ni-Rich 18650-Cells with Si/C Anodes. ChemElectroChem, 11, e202400020. https://doi.org/10.1002/celc.202400020
dataset_metadata.funding: German Federal Ministry of Education and Research, projects Meet Hi-EnD II (03XP0084B) and Meet Hi-EnD III (03XP0258C); research training group mobilEM (GRK 1856/1, 1856/2); BaLD project (03XP0320A)

cell_info.cell_notes: NCA cathode with Ni:Co:Al ratio 8:1:<0.1 and ~3 wt% silicon content in the graphite-silicon anode. Nominal capacity normalized to 3.4 Ah in the publication. Cells bought in March 2018. Initial internal impedance <= 35 mOhm. Max charge current 2.00 A; max discharge current 8.00 A continuous. Charge voltage 4.20 V; discharge cut-off 2.65 V.

aging_modes.notes: 69 cells stored at 5 floating voltage levels (U1–U5) and 4 temperatures (35, 40, 45, 50 °C) in a full-factorial design. Voltage levels correspond to 5 SoC levels at test start: U1=4.054 V (~80% SoC), U2=3.870 V (~59% SoC), U3=3.711 V (~45% SoC), U4=3.510 V (~28% SoC), U5=3.474 V (~25% SoC). Cells held at constant floating voltage (not constant SoC); SoC drifts over time. Number of cells per condition ranges from 2 to 3. EOL RPT protocol applied when cells fail the standard pulse test due to resistance increase.

time_protocol.test_equipment: Digatron MCT 10-06-12ME; Binder MK53 temperature chambers; HAMEG source meters; custom measuring PCB (4-point measurement)
time_protocol.notes: Cells stored continuously at fixed floating voltage in ovens. RPT interval set to 2 months initially, increased to 3 months after 13th RPT (~2 years), then reduced back to 2 months after 19th RPT (~1.5 years later). Total test duration approximately 5 years (~60 months). Up to ~25 RPTs per cell.

rawdata.data_quality_notes: Each RPT has its own file named with a structured scheme (project, specimen, connection, testset, date, test, unique ID, equipment). CSV files use '.' for decimals and ',' as separator with two header rows (column names in German + units). Time format: yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SS. Channel names were renamed after lab relocation (e.g., 'Kreis JS 1-097' = 'Kreis 11-097'). Data available as zipped CSV and MATLAB .mat files.
rawdata.known_issues: Lab relocation in July 2022 caused an interruption (~3.5 weeks at ambient OCV); not all cells completed RPT #19. Some cells at U1 and U3/U4 at 40 °C show data artifacts (possible wrong channel assignment). One cell (Cell G, U2, 45 °C) experienced sudden-death failure at RPT #17 with internal short.

checkup.notes: RPT performed in a Binder temperature chamber at 23 °C. Sequence: (1) discharge to 2.65 V; (2) 10 min rest; (3) CC-CV charge at 0.5C (1.7 A) to 4.20 V, CV until I<0.02C (max 180 min); (4) 30 min rest; (5) 0.5C discharge to 2.65 V (capacity determination); (6) 10 min rest; (7) charge + 30 min rest; (8) quasi-OCV at 0.1C (discharge to 2.65 V and charge to 4.20 V); (9) pulse test at two SoC levels (residual charge 2.6 Ah and 2.1 Ah) using three pulses at 1.7 A, 3.4 A, and 6.8 A (20 s each, charge and discharge directions) with 10 min rest between pulses. Pulse resistance extracted after 2 s from 2C charging pulses at 50% SoC. EOL-RPT omits the higher-SoC pulse stage and reduces qOCV rate to 0.05C. RPT interval was 2 months initially, 3 months from RPT 13 onward, then 2 months again after RPT 19.

notes: Long-term calendaric aging study of Samsung INR18650-35E (NCA/Si-C) cells over 5 years. 69 cells stored at 5 floating voltage levels and 4 temperatures in a full-factorial design. Data published under DOI 10.18154/RWTH-2023-10931. The publication normalizes capacity to 3.4 Ah. Key findings: storage voltage level is the dominant aging driver; temperature influence is modest; aging follows a linear trend after an initial break-in period (~250 days); loss of lithium inventory (LLI) is the main aging mechanism; cathode active material loss detected at highest voltage levels (U1, U2). Post-mortem analyses (SEM/EDX, coin cell cycling) included. Data available from RWTH Aachen publication server (DOI: 10.18154/RWTH-2023-10931).
